paper.title: Bayesian Bandit Beamforming with Implicit Channel Learning for RIS under Hybrid Near/Far-Field Propagation

settings.name_in_paper: Bayesian bandit beamforming for RIS phase-shift configuration (Bayesian received-power regret)
unmapped: Actions are complex unit-modulus vectors b in C^N (|b_n|=1); the dimension N (number of RIS elements) is recorded as d
Reward is the received power |b^T h|^2 (quadratic Hermitian form), but the observation is the noisy linear complex scalar y_t = b_t^T h + xi_t with circular complex Gaussian noise CN(0, sigma^2)
Unknown cascaded channel h drawn from a complex Gaussian prior CN(0, Sigma_0); the learner knows the prior and the noise variance
settings.definition_quote: one scalar pilot observation can be written as y_{t}=\mathbf{b}_{t}^{\top}\mathbf{h}+\xi_{t}. ... \mathcal{R}_{T}\triangleq\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\Big(|\mathbf{b}_{*}^{\top}\mathbf{h}|^{2}-|\mathbf{b}_{t}^{\top}\mathbf{h}|^{2}\Big)\right] where \mathbf{b}_{*}\in\arg\max_{\mathbf{b}\in\mathcal{B}}|\mathbf{b}^{\top}\mathbf{h}|^{2}

algorithms.name: SBL-based Thompson sampling with warm starts

symbols.d: number of RIS elements N (dimension of the channel vector)
symbols.S_h: S = sqrt(E[||h||_2^2]) under the prior (not a norm bound)
symbols.Psi_T: sum_{t=1}^T sqrt(E[tr(Sigma_{t-1})]), cumulative root expected posterior covariance trace

conditions: complex Gaussian prior CN(0, Sigma_0) with Sigma_0 Hermitian positive definite

source.label: thm:Bayesian-regret-decomposition
source.quote: Under the well-specified Bayesian observation model in Sections II-III, assume that $S^{2}\triangleq\mathbb{E}[||\mathbf{h}||_{2}^{2}]<\infty$. The Bayesian regret for the proposed algorithm satisfies \mathcal{R}_{T}\leq4\sqrt{2}NS\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[\text{tr}(\bm{\Sigma}_{t-1})]}

results.notes: Regret decomposition in terms of an algorithm-dependent quantity (posterior covariance trace); received-power Bayesian regret. Effective-rate regret is at most eta/(sigma^2 ln2) times this.

conditions: almost surely lambda_min(G_t) >= C (t - max{t_0,N} + 1) for all t >= max{t_0, N}, for some C>0 (assumption on the realized RIS sequence)

source.label: cor:Sublinear=000020Bayesian=000020regret
source.quote: Assume the well-specified Bayesian observation model and the channel follows Rayleigh fading, $\mathbf{h}\sim\mathcal{CN}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I}_{N})$ ... If there exists a constant $C>0$ such that, almost surely for the realized RIS sequence \lambda_{\min}(\mathbf{G}_{t})\geq C(t-\bar{t}_{0}+1),\forall t\geq\bar{t}_{0}. Then, \mathcal{R}_{T}=O(\sqrt{T}),T\rightarrow\infty.

results.notes: Conditional bound: depends on an assumed linear eigenvalue growth of the algorithm's design matrix, not proved for the algorithm. Initial phase contributes 4*sqrt(2)*N^3 when t_0<=N. Constants depending on N, sigma, C hidden.

symbols.c_alpha: constant c_alpha > 0 in the information-growth condition
symbols.alpha_c: exponent alpha in (1/2,1] of the information-growth condition
symbols.q: q(t) = q_{t,alpha}, probability bound that lambda_min(sum_s Q_s)/t^alpha <= c_alpha

conditions: Rayleigh prior h ~ CN(0, I_N), well-specified model
P(lambda_min(sum_{s<=t} Q_s)/t^alpha <= c_alpha) <= q_{t,alpha} for all t, with Q_t = E[b_t^* b_t^T | F_{t-1}], alpha in (1/2,1], c_alpha > 0

source.label: thm:sublinear=000020comm=000020with=000020channel=000020excitation
source.quote: Suppose that there exist constants $c_{\alpha}>0$ and $\alpha\in(1/2,1]$, and a nonnegative sequence $\{q_{t,\alpha}\}_{t\ge1}$, such that \mathbb{P}(\frac{\lambda_{\min}(\sum_{s=1}^{t}\mathbf{Q}_{s})}{t^{\alpha}}\le c_{\alpha})\le q_{t,\alpha}. Then the cumulative Bayesian received-power regret satisfies ... Consequently, if $\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sqrt{q_{t,\alpha}}=o(T)$, then $\mathcal{R}_{T}/T\to0$

results.notes: Conditional on an information-growth assumption on the algorithm's own sampling, only numerically checked. Theorem also states R_T/T -> 0 if sum sqrt(q_t) = o(T); proof gives O(T^{1-alpha/2}) + O(sum sqrt(q_t)).
